note: Final visual review of the UI overhaul: fifteen reviewers (twelve area units, the phone shell, dark mode and cross-area patterns, motion on the live app) over 962 screenshots of a production build. Shot paths are relative to the capture folder, which is not kept in the repository.

reviews.verdict: This area is now among the most finished parts of the app. On desktop the shell is calm and consistent: sentence-case navigation, group icons, a clear active marker, an account menu that shows who is signed in with a theme control, and a command palette with recent pages and relevant results. On a phone the sign-in flow (brand band with the form rising over it as a sheet) feels like a native app. The bottom bar, the Menu sheet and the quick-action sheet look deliberate, and dark mode holds up everywhere, including the deep-green brand panel. The public pages (OPAC, title detail, document check, offline) now share one frame with the school's identity, and all state pages (404, 403, offline, invalid link, unknown code) share one pattern. What keeps it from a 10 is a handful of edge details. The tab bar is see-through enough that page text sits faintly under its labels. Sheets clip the top border of their first row, and the Menu's recent-pages strip is clipped at the top and cut mid-word at the screen edge. The centre label outweighs the active tab. A few sibling screens differ in small ways (the 403 and 404 pages, the stacked button heights on the sign-in form).
best: Phone sign-in, forgot-password and invalid-link screens: compact brand band with the form rising as a sheet, Manrope titles, one primary action, consistent in light and dark
Desktop account menu: identity block (name, username, role, school, school year), a theme segmented control and Keluar set apart
Command palette: 'Terakhir dibuka' with each page's group on the right, relevant results for 'pre', keyboard hint footer, and the same look in dark mode
Public frame shared by OPAC, title detail, verification and offline: school brand, Katalog and Masuk in the header, a footer, one column width; OPAC rows show availability at a glance
State pages now render inside the shell with one pattern: icon circle, title, one sentence, a primary action and a small error code
worst: Phone tab bar is 85% opaque: the 'Datang' and 'Pulang' text of the card scrolling under it shows faintly beneath the tab labels, in light and dark
Sheets clip the top border of their first row (the quick-action tiles show their top edge missing)
The Menu sheet's recent-pages chips lose their top outline, and the last chip is cut mid-word ('Pengguna d') at the screen edge with no fade
The centre label 'Aksi cepat' is bolder and darker than the active tab, so on the 404 and 403 pages it reads as the selected tab

findings.title: Page text shows through the bottom tab bar under its labels
findings.description: On a phone the bottom bar lets the page scrolling under it stay readable. On the home page the 'Datang' and 'Pulang' labels and the dashes of the Presensi kerja card sit faintly behind 'Beranda', 'Tindakan' and 'Pengguna' (y about 1630 to 1645 in the 2x shot). The same happens in dark mode (mobile-dark/shell__tab-bar--state.png). The labels sit on a noisy ground, which makes the bar look unfinished and costs label contrast on every scrolled page.
findings.cause: apps/web/components/mobile-tab-bar.tsx:161 gives the bar 'bg-surface/85 backdrop-blur-xl backdrop-saturate-150'. That is 15% see-through, and the blur does not wipe out body-size text this close under the bar.
findings.fix: Make the bar opaque: replace 'bg-surface/85 backdrop-blur-xl backdrop-saturate-150' with 'bg-surface'. The 'border-t border-line' hairline already separates it from the page. Update the comment at lines 60-62. If some translucency is wanted, use at least bg-surface/95.

findings.title: Sheet body clips the top edge of its first row
findings.description: In the 'Aksi cepat' sheet, the first row of tiles (Pindai QR, Presensi masuk atau pulang) has rounded top corners but no top border between them: the outline is cut straight off at the top of the scroll area (y about 724 in the 2x shot). Every other tile has its full outline, so the first row looks pasted under the header. The same applies in dark mode, and to the focus ring of any first field or control in a Sheet or Dialog body.
findings.cause: packages/ui/src/components/overlay-parts.tsx:175-176: OverlayBody is 'overflow-y-auto' and gets no top padding when a header is present (only 'padTop && pt-(--dialog-px)'). Anything drawn outside the first child's box is therefore clipped by the scroll container: the tiles' 'ring-1 ring-border' (apps/web/components/mobile-quick-actions.tsx:42) and focus outlines.
findings.fix: In OverlayBody, add 'pt-1' when padTop is false. Take the same 4px off OverlayHeader's 'pb-4' (overlay-parts.tsx:121, change it to 'pb-3') so the header-to-content gap stays 16px. This fixes every Sheet and Dialog at once. A local alternative is to swap 'ring-1 ring-border' for 'border border-border' in QuickActionGrid.

findings.title: Menu sheet's recent-pages chips: top outline clipped, last chip cut mid-word
findings.description: Under 'Terakhir dibuka' the chips (Perlu tindakan, Laporan, Pengguna dan akses) are missing the top of their pill outline: only the corners and the bottom edge show. The third chip runs off the right edge of the screen as 'Pengguna d', a hard cut with no fade, so it looks clipped rather than scrollable. This is the same in dark mode.
findings.cause: apps/web/components/mobile-menu.tsx:157: the strip is '-mx-5 flex gap-2 overflow-x-auto px-5 pb-1 scrollbar-none'. overflow-x-auto also clips vertically, and the chips draw their outline with 'ring-1 ring-border' (line 163) outside their box, with padding only below (pb-1). The strip does not use the shared edge fade.
findings.fix: Change 'pb-1' to 'py-1 -my-1' so the ring has room on both sides. Attach a ref to the ul and call useScrollEdges(ref, { axis: 'x' }) from @newsekolah/ui, then add the shared 'scroll-fade-x' utility (packages/ui/src/styles.css:435), as the tab strips and opac-highlights.tsx already do.

findings.title: Centre action label outweighs the active tab
findings.description: The label under the raised centre button ('Aksi cepat' for admin, 'Pindai' for siswa) is semibold near-black: the heaviest, darkest label in the bar. On the home page it competes with the green active 'Beranda'. On the 404 and 403 pages, where no tab is active, it reads as the selected tab. The raised accent circle already makes the centre the loudest element, so its label does not need extra weight.
findings.cause: apps/web/components/mobile-tab-slot.tsx:148: CENTRE_SLOT adds 'font-semibold'. Line 171 renders the label 'text-fg' whenever the centre is not current.
findings.fix: Give the centre label the same treatment as an inactive tab: drop 'font-semibold' from CENTRE_SLOT and render the label span with slotState(current), which gives 'font-medium text-fg-muted' when idle and 'font-semibold text-accent' when current.

findings.title: 403 and 404 state pages differ in position and button icon
findings.description: Both pages use StatePage, but on the 404 the primary 'Kembali ke beranda' has a house icon and the block sits 24px lower (icon top y 230 against 206 on the 403). On a phone the 404 buttons are inset, while the 403 buttons run to the 16px gutters. Shown one after the other, the two exits look like they were built separately.
findings.cause: apps/web/app/(app)/not-found.tsx wraps StatePage in PageShell and passes icon={<House />}. apps/web/components/forbidden-page.tsx:22-33 renders StatePage without PageShell, and its Button has no icon.
findings.fix: In forbidden-page.tsx, wrap the StatePage in <PageShell> and give the Button icon={<House />}, matching (app)/not-found.tsx. Better still, have both use one small shell state wrapper so they cannot drift again.

findings.title: Stacked full-width sign-in buttons have different heights
findings.description: In the sign-in card on desktop, 'Masuk' is 48px tall and 'Masuk dengan passkey', also full width, is 36px. The second button looks undersized in a narrow column, and the card's bottom half feels uneven.
findings.cause: apps/web/features/auth/components/login-form.tsx:144 sets the submit to size='lg'. apps/web/features/auth/components/passkey-login-button.tsx:53-61 leaves the passkey Button at the default md size.
findings.fix: Pass size='lg' to the Button in passkey-login-button.tsx, and to the Google button if it takes a size, so the stacked actions share one height. The variant still keeps the primary dominant.

findings.title: Rail group chevrons touch their icons
findings.description: In the collapsed rail, the flyout triggers (Akademik, Kesiswaan, Piket dan gerbang, Kepegawaian, Perpustakaan, Data sekolah) carry a small chevron that overlaps the right edge of the 20px icon, most visibly on Kesiswaan's users icon. Those icons also sit off-centre compared with the direct links above the divider.
findings.cause: apps/web/components/sidebar-nav.tsx:309-312: the ChevronRight is 'absolute top-1/2 right-0 size-3' inside a 40px button whose icon spans x 10 to 30, so the chevron (x 28 to 40) overlaps it by 2px.
findings.fix: Move the chevron clear of the icon and make it lighter, for example '-right-1 size-2.5'. The rail column has 12px of padding to take it.

reviews.verdict: The phone frame is mostly well designed. The bar matches docs/17 for every role, the centre action fits each role's day, the pill and centre-current logic are right, and counts sit on the tab they belong to. Dialogs open as real bottom sheets with a handle and a footer you can always reach, and every full page ends well clear of the raised button. Three visible problems bring it down from the owner's bar. The bar is so translucent that page text shows through between and behind the labels on almost every screen, worst in dark. The home stat strip (and the same strip on attendance and library pages) ends in a sliver or a word cut mid-way. The attendance save bar floats 32px above the tab bar with a strip of page between them. One blocker: the library dashboard is wider than the screen, so on a phone the tab bar is pushed off screen for admin, kepsek and pustakawan. Smaller blemishes: sheet tiles lose their top edge, Menu lights up for pages it does not list, some pages have no eyebrow, and some page starts spend whole rows on a lone button.
best: The centre action is right for every role and matches docs/17 (Pindai for siswa and satpam, QR piket, Presensi pointed at the running session, Sirkulasi, Catat, Tindakan for pimpinan, Aksi cepat for admin). Quick actions and menu destinations are both checked with canOpenPath, so I found no remaining case where it leads to a closed page.

Bottom sheets are consistent: grab handle, title on the title role, close button, a scrolling body and a footer that stays in reach, padded for the home indicator, in light and dark (users, years, achievements, visits dialogs).
Content clearance is structural: main pads by --shell-mobile-tab-offset + 16px, and every full-page shot ends 50px or more above the raised button.
The compact header is calm and aligned: brand mark and name, 44px round search, bell and avatar. It matches the page colour until content scrolls under it, and the bell badge reads well.
The active pill, the centre's current state and the per-tab badges are all correct, and drag to dismiss has sensible thresholds (30% capped at 160px, fling 0.5px/ms) with reduced motion handled.
worst: /library (dashboard) is wider than a phone screen: its cards run off the right edge and the fixed tab bar falls out of the visible screen for admin, kepsek and pustakawan.
The tab bar at bg-surface/85 lets page text show through between and behind the labels on nearly every first screen, worst in dark (ghost text contrast about 1.56:1).
The phone stat strip ends in a sliver of a third tile or a label cut mid-word ('Izin keluar menungg', '0 Iz', 'Anggota berbeda h') with no fade.
The attendance save bar sits 32px above the tab bar, leaving a band of page between two pieces of chrome.

findings.title: Library dashboard is wider than a phone screen and pushes the tab bar off screen
findings.description: From the 'Peminjaman dan pengembalian, 30 hari terakhir' card down, every card is wider than the 390px viewport. Titles are cut ('terakhi'), the empty-state sentence is cut ('pengemba'), the 'Terlambat 3..' badges hang off the right edge, and the 'Lihat semua' links are gone. On a phone a page this wide makes the browser widen its layout viewport, so the fixed bottom bar (bottom: 0) ends up below the visible screen. These are the only signed-in phone shots in the whole capture with no tab bar; I checked all 327 fold shots for the centre button, and the other three without it (/monitor and the two library kiosks) are kiosk pages that never have one. The capture's overflow check missed it because innerWidth grows along with the page.
findings.cause: apps/web/features/library/components/library-dashboard-view.tsx:106 `<div className="grid items-start gap-6 lg:grid-cols-3">` has no column template below lg. Its single implicit `auto` track is sized to the widest child's min-content: ListRow titles that do not wrap ('Sapiens: Riwayat Singkat Umat Manusia' plus a badge, dashboard-activity-lists.tsx:115-119). Nothing in the shell stops a page's overflow from widening the phone viewport.
findings.fix: 1) library-dashboard-view.tsx:106 becomes `grid grid-cols-1 items-start gap-6 lg:grid-cols-3`. grid-cols-1 is repeat(1, minmax(0,1fr)), which caps the track, so the ListRow titles truncate as designed. 2) Guard the shell so one page can never take the bar away again. In apps/web/app/globals.css add `@media (width < 48rem) { #main-content { overflow-x: clip; } }`. clip creates no scroll container, so sticky rows and the save bar still work.

findings.title: Tab bar is so translucent that page text reads through its labels
findings.description: Confirmed on almost every first screen. Page text behind the bar stays sharp and legible between and behind the labels: 'Perpustakaan' under Beranda/Jadwal and 'Lihat semua' between Izin and Menu (siswa); 'Presensi kerja' under Tindakan and 'Riwayat' under Menu (guru, light and dark); 'Belum ada pengumuman' under Pindai (satpam); 'Minggu, 15 November' under the check-in bar; 'Pilih tahun ajaran' under Aksi cepat. In the captures the backdrop blur did not apply (the text behind is not blurred at all), so the bar's legibility rests entirely on its 85% opacity. That leaves ghost text at about 1.36:1 against the bar in light and 1.56:1 in dark (green 'Riwayat' at 1.35:1), clearly readable. The opaque top header (bg-bg) and the see-through bottom bar also look like two different materials.
findings.cause: apps/web/components/mobile-tab-bar.tsx:161 `bg-surface/85 backdrop-blur-xl backdrop-saturate-150` (color-mix of --color-surface at 85%). The bar depends on backdrop-filter for legibility and has no opaque fallback. Where the filter is not applied (as in this capture), 15% of the page shows through unblurred.
findings.fix: Preferred: make the bar opaque, matching the opaque header. mobile-tab-bar.tsx:161 becomes `border-t border-line bg-surface`, dropping backdrop-blur and backdrop-saturate. TabBadge's `ring-surface` and the centre's `ring-bg` collar stay correct. If the frosted look is wanted, use `bg-surface/95 backdrop-blur-xl backdrop-saturate-150 not-supports-[backdrop-filter:blur(1px)]:bg-surface`. At 95% the ghost text drops to 1.10:1 (light) and 1.15:1 (dark) even without blur, and to nothing with the 24px --blur-xl. Do not go below 95%.

findings.title: Phone stat strip ends in a sliver or a label cut mid-word, with no fade
findings.description: Confirmed and wider than the home. The bordered strip shows two figures and then either a 4-10px sliver of a third tile (admin, kepsek, guru, pustakawan, siswa homes; on siswa an orange icon edge peeks in) or a label cut mid-word at the card's border: 'Izin keluar menungg' (gurupiket home), '0 Iz' (siswa /attendance), 'Anggota berbeda h' (library visits), 'Tersedia' touching the edge (library dashboard). There is no fade and no deliberate peek, so it looks clipped, not scrollable.
findings.cause: packages/ui/src/components/stat-grid.tsx:89. The scroller is also the bordered card (`overflow-x-auto ... rounded-lg border border-border bg-surface`), with no scroll-fade-x and no useScrollEdges, so nothing marks the cut edge. stat.tsx:75 sizes compact items `min-w-36 flex-1`, so at 342px two figures fill the row and the third starts exactly at the edge.
findings.fix: Split StatStrip into a border box and an inner scroller. Outer: `<div className="overflow-hidden rounded-lg border border-border bg-surface shadow-1">`. Inner, the role=group scroller with the ref: `scrollbar-none overflow-x-auto overscroll-x-contain scroll-fade-x snap-x snap-proximity focus-visible:-outline-offset-2`. Call `useScrollEdges(scrollerRef, { axis: "x" })` (packages/ui/src/hooks/use-scroll-edges.ts), so the existing scroll-fade-x utility (styles.css:435) fades the cut side inside the border, not the border itself. Add `snap-start` to the compact class at stat.tsx:75. For the home only, a 2-column grid on phone (variant 'tiles' below md when there are 4 or fewer tiles, dashboard-view.tsx:245-246) would avoid scrolling altogether.

findings.title: Save bar floats 32px above the tab bar with a band of page between
findings.description: On the teacher's most used screen, the 'Simpan presensi' bar ends at about y 748 (pt) and the tab bar starts at 780. That leaves a 32px strip of page background between two pieces of chrome, and on a longer roster the content scrolls through that strip. It reads as a floating slab, not a bar docked to the bottom chrome.
findings.cause: packages/ui/src/components/sticky-save-bar.tsx:88 puts the bar at `bottom-[var(--shell-mobile-tab-offset)]`. That offset includes --shell-mobile-tab-raise (32px, the centre button's overhang, globals.css:83-86), which only matters in the middle 56px. A sticky form row does the same: globals.css:174-179 `bottom: var(--shell-mobile-tab-offset)`.
findings.fix: Dock the bar on the tab bar and let the raise become its own bottom padding. Then the centre button's overhang lands on the save bar's empty padding, not on the page. StickySaveBar classes: `bottom-[calc(var(--shell-mobile-tab-bar,0px)+env(safe-area-inset-bottom))] pb-[calc(var(--space-3)+var(--shell-mobile-tab-raise,0px))] md:bottom-0 md:pb-3` in place of the current bottom and py-3 bottom. The tab bar comes later in the DOM at the same z-sticky, so the button paints over the padding. Apply the same change to globals.css:176-177: `bottom: calc(var(--shell-mobile-tab-bar) + env(safe-area-inset-bottom)); padding-bottom: calc(var(--space-3) + var(--shell-mobile-tab-raise));`.
alsoOn: settings pages with a save bar
any FormActions sticky on a phone

findings.title: Sheet tiles and recent chips lose their top edge; the recent chip row ends mid-word
findings.description: In the 'Aksi cepat' sheet the first row of tiles ('Pindai QR', 'Presensi masuk atau pulang') has rounded corners but no top border line, so the tiles look sliced, in light and dark. In the Menu sheet the 'Terakhir dibuka' chips lose their top edge the same way. Their row also ends in 'Pengguna c' at the screen edge with no fade.
findings.cause: Both draw their outline as `ring-1 ring-border`, a box-shadow outside the box. Any overflow container clips it. The tiles (apps/web/components/mobile-quick-actions.tsx:43) sit flush at the top of the sheet's `.dialog-body` (overflow-y-auto, overlay-parts.tsx:175, no top padding under a header). The chips (mobile-menu.tsx:163) sit in `ul ... overflow-x-auto` (mobile-menu.tsx:157), which also clips y and has no scroll-fade-x.
findings.fix: Swap the outside ring for an inside border: `border border-border` in place of `ring-1 ring-border` on the QuickActionGrid link (mobile-quick-actions.tsx:43) and on the recent chip (mobile-menu.tsx:163). Give the chip row a fade: add `scroll-fade-x` to the ul at mobile-menu.tsx:157 and call `useScrollEdges(ref, { axis: "x" })` on it. The -mx-5 px-5 bleed can stay.

findings.title: Menu lights up on pages the Menu sheet does not list
findings.description: On 'Presensi saya' (/check-in, reached from the avatar menu) the Menu tab carries the active pill, but opening Menu shows no 'Presensi saya' entry and nothing highlighted, so the bar claims a location it cannot show. The same happens on the student's 'Pindai masuk kelas' (/classroom-entry): Menu is lit while the centre is 'Pindai'. The home hero sends students to /classroom-entry, but the centre opens /scan, which scan-view.tsx:33 calls 'the one scanner for everyone', so a student gets two scanner pages for one task.
findings.cause: apps/web/components/mobile-tab-bar.tsx:96-97 sets `inMenu` for any active entry that is neither a tab nor the centre. That includes items consolidateNavigation marks `sidebarPlacement: "hidden"` (account-menu pages and classroom-entry, lib/navigation-workspaces.ts:311-314), which MobileMenu filters out (mobile-menu.tsx:71).
findings.fix: Light Menu only for entries Menu actually lists. `const activeItem = items.find((item) => item.href === activeHref); const inMenu = activeItem !== undefined && activeItem.sidebarPlacement !== "hidden" && !centreCurrent && !tabs.includes(activeItem);`. Then account pages light nothing, as siswa /announcements already does. For the student, point the hero's 'Pindai masuk kelas' at /scan (the centre's page), or make the centre current on /classroom-entry, so the scanner has one home.

findings.title: Pages without a menu group have no eyebrow, so their title sits higher
findings.description: 'Pengumuman' and 'Perlu tindakan' open with a bare h1 at about y 87 (pt). Every sibling page has an eyebrow ('Akademik', 'Kepegawaian', 'Data sekolah', 'Piket') and its title at about y 108. Moving between Menu pages makes the title jump by one line, and these pages break the template's 'h1 with an eyebrow'.
findings.cause: apps/web/components/app-page.tsx:132-135 takes the eyebrow only from `context.groupKey`. lib/navigation/page-context.ts:74 finds no group for entries without one (announcements at lib/navigation.ts:486-491, and the inbox), and neither view passes `eyebrow`.
findings.fix: Give the ungrouped daily entries an eyebrow. Either add `group: GROUP.communication` to the announcements registry entry and a group to the inbox entry, if the consolidated menu keeps them in the top list regardless. Or pass `eyebrow={t("nav.groups.communication")}` (and a matching key for the inbox, for example 'Kerja harian') from the two views' AppPage.

findings.title: On a phone the table's '...' button takes a whole row of its own when there is no search box
findings.description: On Tahun ajaran the toolbar shows a lone '...' at the right of an otherwise empty 44px row, then the filter chip on its own row. With the 4-line description, the primary button row and the tabs, the only card starts at y 460 of 844, more than half the first screen. The library visits page has the same lone '...' row above its date-range filter chip.
findings.cause: packages/ui/src/components/data-table/data-table-toolbar.tsx:244-261. Filters are `order-4 basis-full` on a phone, and the view-options group is `order-2 ml-auto`. Without a search box (showSearch false), nothing shares the overflow menu's row.
findings.fix: When there is no search box, put the pills beside the overflow menu on a phone. Change the DataTableFilters className at line 248 to `cn("order-4 basis-full md:order-2 md:min-w-48 md:flex-1 md:basis-0", !showSearch && "max-md:order-1 max-md:min-w-0 max-md:flex-1 max-md:basis-0")`. The '...' (order-2) then ends the chip row.

findings.title: The primary action takes a whole row under the title on a phone
findings.description: 'Buat pengumuman', 'Tambah tahun ajaran', 'Catat prestasi' and 'Catat kunjungan' each sit alone on a 44px row, half its width, between the title and the tabs. The right half is empty, and the page head grows by about 56px before any content. Meanwhile the secondary '...' already sits neatly at the end of the title line. A phone app puts its one add action in the title line.
findings.cause: packages/ui/src/components/page-header.tsx:248-255. On a phone `primaryAction` always goes in the actions row under the heading block (`phoneActions`), while the overflow menu is placed in the heading grid's trailing column (lines 229-234).
findings.fix: Add an optional compact form of the primary action to PageHeader and AppPage, for example `primaryActionCompact?: { icon: ReactNode; label: string; onSelect?: () => void; href?: string }`. Below sm, render it in the heading grid's trailing column as a 44px accent IconButton (`aria-label` = label, beside the overflow button). From sm up, keep the full button. When there are no free-form `actions`, the phone actions row then disappears. Adopt it on list pages whose primary is Tambah/Buat/Catat.

findings.title: Drag to dismiss can swallow the first upward scroll of a sheet at its top
findings.description: This is a risk read from the code; a still image cannot show it. In the long Menu sheet (or any sheet) scrolled to its top, a swipe up that starts with a 0-2px downward jitter can stall, because the first touchmove is cancelled. iOS Safari and Chrome then do not scroll for that touch, and the reader has to swipe again. Thresholds (30% of height capped at 160px, a 0.5px/ms flick after 24px), scroll lock (Radix) and reduced motion (snap back; a dismissed sheet fades where it is) are otherwise sound.
findings.cause: packages/ui/src/components/overlay-drag.ts:203-213. While deciding, any touchmove with dy >= 0 and |dx| <= |dy| on a body scrolled to the top calls `event.preventDefault()` (line 212), including dy = 0 and moves still under the 8px slop. Cancelling the first touchmove of a sequence cancels native scrolling for the whole gesture.
findings.fix: For touches that start in the body (`start.body` set), do not cancel before the gesture is clearly a downward drag. Return without preventDefault while `dy < SHEET_DRAG.slop` or `dy <= Math.abs(dx)`, and only then claim it (preventDefault and dragging = true). Keep the current early preventDefault only for touches on the handle and header (`start.body === null`). At the top of the body, OverlayBody's `overscroll-contain` already keeps those few pixels from moving the page behind.
alsoOn: every Dialog and Sheet on a phone

reviews.verdict: This area improved a lot and now mostly looks like one product. Every route sits on the AppPage template. The session editor is the strongest screen: two-line header, joined H/S/I/D/A control, compact sticky counts, first student at about 335px on a phone. The gradebook now opens with the sheet, the phone schedule is a clean time-led agenda with a real bottom-sheet form, and /my-grades with its KKTP meter is what the bar asks for. Dark mode holds up on attendance, grading and schedule. What drops it from 8 to 7 is one shared regression and a group of hierarchy slips. On a phone, the summary strip (StatGrid strip) cuts its third figure in half at the screen edge on four screens, with no fade, where the old 2x2 tiles showed every figure. The journal leaves an empty 22rem column on desktop for anyone without a backlog, shows a full-width "Unduh" bar above search on a phone, and repeats its primary "Jurnal baru" inside the empty state (substitutions does the same with "Minta pengganti"). The copy is also uneven: times read "07:00-07:45" in the grid but "07.00 – 23.59" everywhere else, homeroom says "Alpa" where the rest of the area says "Alpha", and the student calendar's "Belum lengkap" dot is grey while its badge is orange.
best: /attendance/[sessionId] on desktop and phone: two-line header, joined status control, compact sticky counts, save bar aligned to the gutter, first student well above the fold
/my-grades (siswa): large score with a KKTP meter, Indonesian decimal comma, calm card grid
/schedule on a phone: one-row week picker, time-led lesson cards, the 'Tambah jadwal' form as a proper bottom sheet with its buttons visible
/grading (guru desktop): sheet first, one summary strip, visible 'Tambah komponen', publish state in one place
Role-aware empty states on /grading (kepsek, gurupiket) and /schedule (gurubk) that explain and offer a next step
worst: Phone summary strips (/attendance siswa, /grading guru, /homeroom guru, /my-grades siswa) cut the third figure in half at the right edge with no fade
/journal desktop for admin, kepsek, gurubk and gurupiket: the table stops at about 1040px with an empty 22rem rail column beside it
/journal and /substitutions: the same primary action twice on one screen (header and empty state)
/journal on a phone: a full-width secondary 'Unduh' bar is the first content under the tabs, and the toolbar takes three rows
Mixed time formats on one screen in /schedule ('13:45-18:00' pill and grid, '07.00 / 23.59' card, 'Jam 1 (07:00)' form)

findings.title: Phone summary strip cuts its third figure in half at the screen edge
findings.description: At 390px the StatGrid strip shows two figures and then a third cut mid-word at the card's right edge, with no fade, peek padding or other hint that it scrolls. On /attendance (siswa) the third figure reads '0 Iz'; on /grading (guru) only the third tile's check icon shows; on /homeroom (guru) only the 'Belum lengkap' icon; on /my-grades (siswa) '1 N...'. Before the overhaul these were 2x2 tiles and every figure was visible, so on a phone this is a regression.
findings.cause: packages/ui/src/components/stat-grid.tsx:82-93: StatStrip is `scrollbar-none overflow-x-auto` with the border and surface on the scroller itself, and the dl is `flex w-max min-w-full` while each compact Stat has `min-w-36` (stat.tsx:75). Four or five 144px+ items overflow a 358px phone width, and the strip does not use the `scroll-fade-x` + useScrollEdges treatment that tab-styles.tsx:43 uses.
findings.fix: Below sm, lay the strip out as a two-column grid so up to four figures all show: dl className `grid grid-cols-2 sm:flex sm:w-max sm:min-w-full sm:divide-x sm:divide-line`, and give compact Stats `max-sm:[&:nth-child(odd)]:border-r max-sm:[&:nth-child(-n+2)]:border-b border-line max-sm:min-w-0`. Keep the sideways scroll from sm up only. If a strip has five or more figures, move the border and surface to an outer div and put `scroll-fade-x` with useScrollEdges on an inner scroller, like the tabs do.

findings.title: Times written two ways, sometimes on the same screen
findings.description: On the phone schedule, the current-period pill reads 'Jam 9 13:45-18:00' (colon, hyphen) while the lesson card below reads '07.00 / 23.59' (dot). The desktop grid's period column uses '07:00-07:45', the 'Tambah jadwal' form shows 'Jam 1 (07:00)', and /attendance and the session header use '07.00 – 23.59' (dot, spaced en dash). The same form also uses a bare 'Pilih' placeholder for Mata pelajaran and Guru.
findings.cause: apps/web/features/schedule/period-span.ts:17-19 formatPeriodTime returns `HH:MM-HH:MM`, used by schedule-current-period-pill.tsx:37 and schedule-grid-cells.tsx:138. schedule-form.tsx:104 builds `${p.name} (${p.starts_at.slice(0, 5)})`. Neither goes through clockLabel/clockRange (features/schedule/clock-label.ts), which the rest of the area uses.
findings.fix: Make formatPeriodTime take `locale` and return `clockRange(period.starts_at, period.ends_at, locale)`, then pass useLocale() at both call sites. In schedule-form.tsx use `${p.name} (${clockLabel(p.starts_at, locale)})`. Replace the generic `t("pick")` placeholders (schedule-form.tsx:168,177) with 'Pilih mata pelajaran' and 'Pilih guru'.

reviews.verdict: This area is far better than before the overhaul. Every page now uses the template, the copy is in sentence case Indonesian, the date and time pickers are real components, dialogs open as proper bottom sheets on a phone, and the desktop list pages (billing desk, staff attendance board, supervision cycles, the visitors board and its sibling tabs) look calm and professional in both themes. The observation form on desktop is the best screen here: a narrow column, a scale legend and a running count in a sticky save bar. The weak spot is the supervision detail screens that nobody had seen before. On the cycle detail the compact stepper is squeezed until its labels run together, and on a phone its summary strip pushes a label across the divider into the next figure and cuts off the third figure at the card edge. On the phone observation form the save bar floats 32px above the tab bar, and the page shows through the gap. The known visitors board defect is not fixed: on a phone the search and the segmented control run to the right screen edge, and on desktop the search shrinks until its placeholder is cut off. Across the visitors pages, the empty states repeat the header's primary button, and on a phone the date controls stack above the tabs, so the tab row jumps between sibling pages. The bones are good, but the phone and detail views still look visibly uneven against the owner's bar.

findings.title: Summary strip cells do not grow to their labels: text crosses the divider and figures are cut at the card edge
findings.description: In the phone summary strip on the cycle detail, the label 'Observasi terjadwal' runs past its cell, across the vertical divider, almost to the 'Guru' icon. The third cell (purple 'Kriteria' icon) is sliced in half by the card's right edge, and the fourth ('Skala') is hidden. Nothing shows that the strip scrolls: no fade, no peek. The component's own comment says 'A strip cell grows to its label instead of cutting it', but it does not. On /homeroom the third strip cell is also cut off by the edge without a fade.
findings.cause: packages/ui/src/components/stat.tsx:75 makes the compact cell 'min-w-36 flex-1'. flex-1 means flex-basis 0, and the explicit min-width replaces the content-based minimum, so each cell is held at 144px whatever its nowrap label (stat.tsx:258) needs. The dl's 'w-max min-w-full' (stat-grid.tsx:93) then adds up these too-narrow cells. stat-grid.tsx:89 puts the border and background on the scroller itself and never uses useScrollEdges or scroll-fade-x, so a cut figure gets no fade.
findings.fix: In stat.tsx:75 change compact to 'relative flex min-w-36 flex-[1_0_auto] flex-col justify-center py-3 pr-5 pl-4'. With basis auto and no shrink, a cell is at least its icon padding plus its label, and the strip scrolls when the cells do not fit. In stat-grid.tsx, move the border, radius, background and shadow onto an outer wrapper. Give the inner scroller 'scroll-fade-x' and call useScrollEdges(scrollerRef, { axis: 'x' }), as the SegmentedControl and tab strips do, so a figure past the edge fades out instead of being sliced.

findings.title: Cycle step strip is squeezed to about 230px: labels run together and 'Lihat hasil' wraps

'Instrumen' and 'Jadwalkan' sit edge to edge with no gap, reading as one phrase, and 'Lihat hasil' breaks over two lines. The labels are not centred under their markers. The phone version shows the same collision.
findings.cause: apps/web/features/supervision/components/supervision-cycle-detail-view.tsx:167 passes <Stepper variant="compact"> as the AppPage toolbar. PageShell renders the toolbar as 'flex min-w-0 flex-wrap items-center gap-2' (packages/ui/src/components/page-shell.tsx:146), so the stepper's ol is a content-sized flex item. Its li are 'flex-1 min-w-0' (stepper.tsx:152), so each collapses below the width of its label.
findings.fix: Give the stepper a width: <Stepper variant="compact" className="w-full max-w-lg" ...> in supervision-cycle-detail-view.tsx:167, or render it in the body above the StatGrid instead of in the toolbar. Each step then gets about 120px and the labels sit centred under their markers on one line.

findings.title: Sticky save bar floats above the tab bar, and the page shows through the gap
findings.description: On a phone, 'Simpan hasil observasi' sits in a white bar that ends about 32px above the bottom tab bar. In that band, the next criterion's score buttons (1 2 3 4) show between the two fixed bars, and the raised 'Aksi cepat' button sits on top of them. Two stacked fixed surfaces with live content between them look broken. The translucent tab bar also shows faint page text through 'Beranda'.
findings.cause: packages/ui/src/components/sticky-save-bar.tsx:88 anchors the bar at bottom: var(--shell-mobile-tab-offset). apps/web/app/globals.css:84 defines that offset as bar + raise + safe area, and the 2rem raise is only the centre button's overhang, not a surface. The same offset drives sticky FormActions (globals.css:176), which have the same gap.
findings.fix: Anchor the save bar on the tab bar itself and let its surface cover the raise. Use bottom: calc(var(--shell-mobile-tab-bar) + env(safe-area-inset-bottom)) and padding-bottom: calc(var(--space-3) + var(--shell-mobile-tab-raise)) below md, keeping md:bottom-0. The save button stays above the centre button, which now rests on the bar's own surface. Apply the same change to the sticky FormActions rule in globals.css:176.

findings.title: Board toolbar is not constrained: it runs to the phone's edge and truncates the search on desktop (known issue, not fixed)
findings.description: On a 390px phone (all roles), the search field and the Semua / Di sekolah / Terjadwal control both end about 1px from the right screen edge. The left side keeps its 16px gutter. On desktop the same toolbar shrinks the search to about 200px, its placeholder is cut mid-word ('Cari nama atau instans'), and 'justify-between' has no effect.
findings.cause: apps/web/features/visitors/components/gate-board-view.tsx:158 wraps the toolbar in 'flex flex-col gap-3 sm:flex-row sm:items-center sm:justify-between' without a width. Inside PageShell's 'flex flex-wrap' toolbar row (page-shell.tsx:146), that wrapper is a content-sized flex item with min-width:auto. It takes the min-content width of the SegmentedControl, whose radio group is 'w-full min-w-max' with three equal columns (segmented-control.tsx:151), about 373px, wider than the 358px column. On desktop the search's 'sm:flex-1' inside a content-sized box falls to its minimum.
findings.fix: In gate-board-view.tsx:158 add 'w-full min-w-0' to the wrapper: 'flex w-full min-w-0 flex-col gap-3 sm:flex-row sm:items-center sm:justify-between'. On a phone the segmented track (w-full) then scrolls inside 358px with its own edge fades. On desktop the search takes its max-w-sm and the segmented control sits at the right end.

findings.title: Two identical primary buttons in view: header action repeated in the empty state

reviews.verdict: The home is a real step up. Every role now opens on one hero with one clear action, calm states included. Cards share one radius, one header style and accent text links. Dark mode uses the bright token accent, and on the phone the header, the one-line greeting and the bottom bar finally feel like an app. Two things let it down. First, the phone stat strip ends in a clipped sliver on six of nine homes (cut mid-word for guru piket) and hides half the figures with no hint. Second, the home says the same fact three or four times (hero, tile, queue card), worst on calm days. On desktop, the side check-in card puts a second, louder primary button next to the hero's. The satpam home is a hero plus one half-width notification tile, and the leadership homes are lopsided. /check-in has a sound structure, but its copy is unfinished: "Jadwal belum diatur" appears nine times, rows read "– – –", and an alert tells the admin to contact the admin. /announcements is clean and consistent, but only its empty state was captured.

findings.title: Phone stat strip ends in a clipped sliver and hides half the figures
findings.description: On the phone home the stat strip is one rounded card that scrolls sideways, and its right edge falls wherever the labels happen to end. Admin, kepsek and pustakawan show the second cell's label running to a stray divider with about 7px of a third cell. Siswa shows the edge of a pink icon circle. Guru piket shows the label cut mid-word: 'Izin keluar menungg'. There is no fade, no snap and no peek large enough to read as a card, so this reads as a clipping bug, not a scroll hint. The figures past the edge are effectively invisible: Pengguna aktif and Sedang daring (admin, kepsek), Presensi kelas and Notifikasi (guru), Dikembalikan and Kunjungan (pustakawan), Buku dipinjam and Mapel bernilai (siswa).
findings.cause: apps/web/features/dashboard/components/dashboard-view.tsx:245-251 chooses StatGrid variant 'strip' on every phone, whatever the tile count. packages/ui/src/components/stat-grid.tsx:89-92: the scroller is overflow-x-auto inside a rounded border, with `dl` set to `flex w-max min-w-full`, and has no snap, edge padding or fade. packages/ui/src/components/stat.tsx:75 sets compact cells to `min-w-36 flex-1`, and stat.tsx:259 sets their labels to `whitespace-nowrap`, so each cell's width follows its label length and the viewport edge lands at an arbitrary point (on a divider, on an icon or mid-word).
findings.fix: For the home (at most 4 figures), lay the phone strip out as a 2x2 compact grid with no scrolling. Add a `wrap` option to StatStrip that renders the `dl` as `grid grid-cols-2` with hairlines (`[&>*:nth-child(even)]:border-l [&>*:nth-child(n+3)]:border-t border-line`) instead of `flex w-max divide-x`, and pass it from dashboard-view.tsx when `!isDesktop && tiles.length <= 4`. That is two rows of about 62px, so every figure is visible. Keep the scroller only for 5 or more figures: add `snap-x snap-mandatory` on the scroller, give cells `snap-start shrink-0 basis-[42%]` so the next cell deliberately peeks by about 40%, and add a trailing mask fade (`[mask-image:linear-gradient(to_right,#000_calc(100%-32px),transparent)]`) while `overflows` is true and the scroller is not at its end.

findings.title: Each home states the same fact three or four times

findings.cause: The blocks add tiles and queue cards regardless of what the hero already says. apps/web/features/dashboard/home/blocks/picket.tsx:137-150 always pushes PicketQueueCard. counselor.tsx:170-184 pushes counselor.queue and deputy.tsx:97-100 pushes deputy.queues even when they are all empty. leadership.tsx:104-126 gives the hero a title, a meta and a progress label with valueLabel for one number, and leadership.tsx:153-163 adds the same figure as the school.sessions tile. librarian.tsx:59-99 states loans, returns and overdue in both the hero and the tiles.

findings.title: Leadership and BK homes are lopsided: short main column, long side column

findings.title: Check-in page: 'Jadwal belum diatur' nine times, '– – –' rows, admin told to contact admin
findings.description: The today card shows a 'Jadwal belum diatur' badge, then the warning 'Jadwal kerja Anda belum diatur. Hubungi admin untuk mengaturnya.' (also shown to the admin), then every one of the seven rows repeats the same badge. Every row's meta reads '– – –'. reviews.verdict: These five screens are a big step up from before. Every page now sits in the shared template: a trail or back link, one h1 with a description, section tabs, then content. The approval-flow editor went from a wall of form cards to collapsible stage rows with a live summary, an undo toast and a save bar. Security finally matches its name, and SSO has a proper three-state status. What keeps it below 8 is the frame. Settings pages under one section use different widths: session and SSO are narrow and centred, while WhatsApp, workflows and audit are default width and left-aligned. So the title and the section tab strip jump 216px sideways as you click between sibling tabs. On top of that, the WhatsApp page still feels unfinished: its activation switch floats in the middle of the card, and its save button differs from every other settings form. Smaller blemishes: a status card that only repeats the page title (SSO), a passkey empty state that outweighs the real 2FA control, and a "Lama sesi / Lama sesi" title and label pair. Method: all 36 security shots (9 roles x desktop/phone x fold/full) were checked with a pixel diff of the content area against admin's; the content is identical, and 8 of them were looked at by eye. All other shots were looked at by eye. No dark shots exist for this unit. The document-template detail route was reviewed from code only.
best: Approval-flow editor (/settings/workflows): numbered collapsible stage rows, a version badge, a summary Stepper beside the list, the stage code tucked under 'Lanjutan', remove with undo, and a save bar that confirms the new version
Security (/settings/security): titled 'Keamanan akun' to cover its content, one primary action, each card titled by its feature with a status badge, and a link card to password and sessions
SSO: three-state badge ('Belum diatur'), no switch until configured, 'Simpan dan aktifkan' in the save bar, field-level validation
The template is applied evenly: breadcrumb on desktop, '< Pengaturan sekolah' back link on the phone, section tabs that fit or fade at the edge, last content always clear of the bottom bar
Session: NumberInput with a 'hari' suffix, and the shared SettingSwitchRow with the switch on the right
worst: The h1 and the section tab strip jump 216px sideways between sibling settings tabs (narrow centred vs default left-aligned), and the template list to editor jumps the same way
WhatsApp 'Aktifkan pengiriman WhatsApp' switch floats mid-card in a 14rem label grid, with its hint stranded under it
The WhatsApp provider keeps an always-on in-card 'Simpan' while every sibling uses the sticky save bar with leave protection
The SSO first card only repeats the page title ('Masuk dengan Google' appears four times in 230px) around one callout
The passkey empty state is a full centred block (about 320px) that outweighs the 2FA card above it

findings.title: Header and section tabs jump 216px sideways between sibling settings tabs
findings.description: On 'Sesi dan masuk' and 'Masuk dengan Google', the trail, the h1 and the underline tab strip start at x=480 in a centred 720px column, and the strip ends at x=1200. Click the third tab, 'Jejak audit', and the same header and strip start at x=264 and run to x=1416. The same happens in the communication section: 'Notifikasi bawaan' sits at x=480, while 'WhatsApp' and 'Integrasi' sit at x=264. The template list (narrow) and the template editor (default) jump the same way. The tab strip you just clicked moves out from under the cursor. The strip also moves down 20px on SSO because its description wraps to two lines while its siblings' take one. The settings area therefore feels like separate pages, not one workspace. docs/07 asks that switching sections not replace the header.
findings.cause: apps/web/features/settings/components/settings-page.tsx:35 defaults every settings page to variant="narrow", which PageShell centres with mx-auto max-w-narrow (packages/ui/src/components/page-shell.tsx:26-28, 109). whatsapp-settings-view.tsx:25, workflow-definitions-view.tsx:172, integrations-view.tsx:26 and template-editor.tsx:62 pass variant="default", and audit-logs-view.tsx:220 passes "fit". At 1440px these fill the content area and so read as left-aligned. The SSO description (messages/features/sso.id.json "description", 117 characters) wraps inside max-w-prose.
findings.fix: Give every settings page the same frame and narrow only the content. In SettingsPage, pass AppPage variant={variant === "narrow" ? "default" : variant}, and for narrow pages pass contentClassName={cn("w-full max-w-narrow", contentClassName)}. Default SettingsSaveBar's container to "default" so the bar lines up with the header. In whatsapp-settings-view.tsx:32, replace md:max-w-2xl with max-w-narrow. Title, trail and tabs then start at x=264 on every settings tab and on the template editor, and forms keep their 720px column. Shorten the SSO description to one line, e.g. 'Izinkan staf dan guru masuk dengan akun Google Workspace sekolah.'

findings.title: WhatsApp activation switch floats mid-card with its hint stranded beneath it
findings.description: Every other field in the 'Penyedia pengiriman' card is a full-width vertical field. The 'Aktifkan pengiriman WhatsApp' row instead puts its label in a left column (x=285). The switch floats at x=533, about 8px higher than the label, and the hint 'Saat nonaktif, ...' wraps in the right column some 30px below the switch. On the phone the switch drops under the label, left-aligned. On Sesi dan masuk and Masuk dengan Google the same kind of setting has the label and hint on the left and the switch on the right. This row looks broken at a glance.
findings.cause: apps/web/features/messaging/components/provider-config-view.tsx:180-187 uses <Field orientation="horizontal">. That draws a grid of a 14rem label column plus a control column (packages/ui/src/components/field.tsx:220-221) inside a form that is otherwise vertical, rather than the shared SettingSwitchRow.
findings.fix: Replace the Field with <SettingSwitchRow label={t("activeLabel")} hint={t("activeHint")} checked={form.isActive} onCheckedChange={(checked) => setForm((f) => ({ ...f, isActive: checked }))} /> from features/settings/components/setting-switch-row.tsx, as session-settings-view.tsx:131 and sso-view.tsx:165 do.

findings.title: WhatsApp provider keeps its own always-on 'Simpan' instead of the settings save bar
findings.description: The provider form ends with a primary 'Simpan', at the right edge of the card on desktop and full width on the phone. It is enabled with nothing changed, and leaving the page with edits does not ask first. Session, SSO, the workflow editor and the template editor show nothing until something changes, then raise the shared bar ('Ada perubahan yang belum disimpan', 'Batalkan', 'Simpan perubahan') with leave protection. The provider view also has no error state: a failed load shows the empty default form, which a save would write back.
findings.cause: apps/web/features/messaging/components/provider-config-view.tsx:189-193 renders FormActions with its own Button and keeps no dirty state. Lines 77-79 handle only isLoading, not isError.
findings.fix: Move the form state into a hook (e.g. useProviderConfigForm) that WhatsAppSettingsView calls. Pass floating={<SettingsSaveBar dirty={dirty} saving={save.isPending} onSave={handleSave} onDiscard={reseed} />} to its SettingsPage while the Penyedia panel is active; the bar is position-fixed, so it must sit in the floating slot outside the entering content. Remove FormActions. Before the skeleton, add `if (query.isError && !query.data) return <QueryError retry={() => query.refetch()} error={query.error} />` as session and SSO do.

findings.title: SSO status card repeats the page title and holds a single callout
findings.description: 'Masuk dengan Google' appears four times in the top 230px: the last crumb, the h1, the active tab, and the title of the first card. That card, about 150px tall on desktop and 180px on the phone, holds only the 'Belum diatur' badge and a blue info callout. The real work, the credentials card, starts below it.
findings.cause: apps/web/features/sso/components/sso-view.tsx:163-176 always renders a FormSection card titled t("statusTitle"), which is 'Masuk dengan Google' in messages/features/sso.id.json. When the integration is not configured, its only child is the Alert.
findings.fix: When !data.configured, render the Alert as the first child of the credentials FormSection (sso-view.tsx:178), with no card of its own. Pass statusBadge to SettingsPage `actions` so it sits beside the h1. Keep the switch card only once configured, and retitle statusTitle to something that is not the page name, e.g. 'Di halaman masuk'.

findings.title: Passkey empty state is larger than the 2FA control it sits under
findings.description: The Passkey card is 322px tall on desktop and about 350px on the phone. Most of it is a centred fingerprint circle, 'Belum ada passkey', a sentence that restates the card description, and an outlined button. That is twice the height of the 'Verifikasi dua langkah' card, the page's main control. On the phone the first screen ends in the middle of this block, so 'Tambah passkey' and the password and sessions link are below the fold.
findings.cause: apps/web/features/security/components/passkeys-section.tsx:192-197 renders EmptyState with no variant, so inside a Card it becomes 'inline' (px-6 py-8, md icon circle; packages/ui/src/components/empty-state.tsx:53).
findings.fix: Use <EmptyState variant="compact" className="px-5 pb-5" icon={<Fingerprint />} title={t("emptyTitle")} action={addButton("secondary")} /> and drop the description, which the card description already says. The card becomes one row with the button at its end.

findings.title: 2FA button glued to a status sentence that repeats the badge and the description
findings.description: In 'Verifikasi dua langkah', the green 'Aktifkan verifikasi dua langkah' sits about 6px under 'Belum aktif. Setelah diaktifkan, masuk memerlukan kode dari aplikasi autentikator selain kata sandi.', while the gap above that sentence is about 20px. The sentence itself repeats the 'Tidak aktif' badge and the card description line just above it.
findings.cause: apps/web/features/security/components/security-view.tsx:121 wraps the body in a raw <div className="flex flex-col gap-3 px-5"> with no bottom padding. The following CardFooter adds only pt-1 (packages/ui/src/components/card.tsx:195), because it expects CardContent's 20px. The copy is status.disabledBody in messages/features/security.id.json.
findings.fix: Replace the div with <CardContent className="flex flex-col gap-3">, which gives 20+4px before the footer. Render the status paragraph only when data.confirmed, or replace disabledBody with something new, e.g. 'Disarankan untuk akun dengan akses data sekolah.'

findings.title: Session page: two cards for two controls, with a card title that repeats its field label
findings.description: The first card is titled 'Lama sesi' and its only field is labelled 'Lama sesi'. The second card, 'Perangkat', holds a single switch. Two framed cards with headings for two settings fragment a page that is one short form.
findings.cause: apps/web/features/settings/components/session-settings-view.tsx:118-138 renders two FormSection cards, and app.settings.session.sessionTitle equals daysLabel ('Lama sesi') in messages/id.json.
findings.fix: Put the NumberInput field and the SettingSwitchRow in one FormSection variant="card" titled e.g. 'Aturan sesi', and delete sessionTitle and devicesTitle. If two cards stay, retitle the first 'Masa berlaku' so it no longer equals the field label.

findings.title: WhatsApp on the phone: two tab rows, then a card header that names the tab again
findings.description: Under the h1 and its description, the phone shows the underline strip 'Notifikasi bawaan | WhatsApp | Integrasi', then the pill strip 'Penyedia | Templat | Log pengiriman', then a 36px gap, then a card titled 'Penyedia pengiriman' with a three-line paragraph. The first input starts about 507px down an 844px screen. On desktop the pill-to-card gap is 38px, against 24px for the same pattern on Alur persetujuan. The chosen panel is not in the URL, so a reload or the back button always returns to 'Penyedia'.
findings.cause: apps/web/features/messaging/components/whatsapp-settings-view.tsx:26 uses <Tabs defaultValue="provider" className="... gap-5">, and TabsContent adds pt-4 by default (packages/ui/src/components/tabs.tsx:159). provider-config-view.tsx:102-105 repeats the panel name as a CardTitle.
findings.fix: Keep the panel in the URL with useUrlState("panel", ["provider","templates","deliveries"], "provider") and value/onValueChange, as workflow-definitions-view.tsx:63 does. Use gap-6 on Tabs and className="pt-0" on each TabsContent to match workflows. In the provider card, drop the CardTitle and keep the sentence as a CardDescription. The first field rises about 60px on the phone.

findings.title: Flow summary reads as disabled and orders who and how differently from the rows
findings.description: In 'Ringkasan alur', every stage name ('Guru piket', 'Guru BK', 'Pimpinan') is in muted grey beside an outlined grey disc, so the active flow looks pending or switched off. Each step shows the method first ('Pindai QR') and the approver after ('Guru mana pun'), while the stage rows beside it say 'Guru mana pun · Pindai QR' and the card hint promises 'Siapa ... dan caranya'. On the phone this card repeats the three rows right above it as another 340px block.
findings.cause: apps/web/features/workflows/components/stage-editor.tsx:214-224 passes currentIndex={-1} and state "upcoming" to Stepper, which mutes upcoming labels (packages/ui/src/components/stepper.tsx:209), and maps description to the verification method and actor to the approver rule.
findings.fix: In stage-editor.tsx, pass description: ruleLabel(item.stage.approver_rule) and actor: t(`stage.verification.${...}`) so the order matches the rows. In stepper.tsx:209, mute only when the stepper shows progress: `state === "upcoming" && currentIndex >= 0 ? "text-fg-muted" : "text-fg"`. Show the summary card from lg up only (`hidden lg:block` on the Card at stage-editor.tsx:205), since on the phone the rows already say the same.

findings.title: Four look-alike icon controls at the end of each stage row
findings.description: Each stage row ends in a grey expand chevron, an up arrow, a down arrow and a '...' menu, all 16px glyphs about 36px apart. Up and down appear a second time inside the '...' menu. The chevron, which opens the stage for editing, is the faintest of the four.
findings.cause: apps/web/features/workflows/components/stage-row.tsx:135-155 renders inline IconButtons for move up and down from sm up, and the RowActionsMenu at 89-111 lists the same two moves again.
findings.fix: Keep one place for reordering: remove the sm:flex IconButton group (stage-row.tsx:135-155) and leave the moves in the menu, or keep the arrows and remove moveUp and moveDown from the menu items.

findings.title: Card inset is 24px on session and SSO, 20px on security, WhatsApp and workflows
findings.description: On desktop, card titles sit 24px inside the card edge on Sesi dan masuk and Masuk dengan Google ('Lama sesi' at x=505 in a card starting at x=481). On Keamanan akun, WhatsApp and Alur persetujuan they sit 20px in ('Verifikasi dua langkah' at x=501). Moving between settings pages, the content inset shifts by 4px.
findings.cause: packages/ui/src/components/form-layout.tsx:57 gives FormSection variant="card" `p-5 md:p-6`, while Card, CardHeader and CardContent use p-5 at every width (packages/ui/src/components/card.tsx:42, 137, 184).
findings.fix: Change form-layout.tsx:57 to `p-5` so FormSection cards share Card's 20px inset at every width.

findings.title: WhatsApp secret field differs from SSO's: status shown as a placeholder, no reveal toggle
findings.description: 'Token akses' shows the placeholder 'Belum diisi', which reads as a status rather than a hint, while 'ID nomor telepon' just above it is blank. Once a token is saved, the placeholder becomes 'Tersimpan — kosongkan untuk tetap memakai token ini', which will be cut off in the phone field. SSO handles the same write-only secret with a PasswordInput (eye toggle), the placeholder 'Tidak diubah' and the explanation as a hint.
findings.cause: apps/web/features/messaging/components/provider-config-view.tsx:130-143 (and 163-176 for the gateway header) uses <Input type="password"> and puts the status sentences from messages/features/messaging.id.json (accessTokenPlaceholderSet and Unset) in the placeholder.
findings.fix: Follow sso-view.tsx:195-207: use PasswordInput, set the placeholder to 'Tidak diubah' when has_access_token and empty otherwise, and move 'Kosongkan untuk mempertahankan token yang tersimpan.' into the Field hint. Do the same for the gateway header value.

findings.title: Client ID placeholder cut mid-word on the phone
findings.description: On the phone the Client ID field shows 'xxxxxxxxxx.apps.googleusercontent.c', cut at the right edge of the input.
findings.cause: messages/features/sso.id.json clientIdPlaceholder is 37 characters, more than the roughly 294px text box on a 390px screen can show.
findings.fix: Drop the placeholder and give the format as a hint instead, e.g. clientIdHint 'Berakhiran .apps.googleusercontent.com', passed as Field hint in sso-view.tsx:184.

findings.title: Page description leaves a one-word last line
findings.description: The security description wraps with 'masuk.' alone on its second line on both desktop and the phone. Single-word last lines under the h1 look unset.
findings.cause: packages/ui/src/components/page-header.tsx:238: the description container has max-w-prose but no text-wrap balancing.
findings.fix: Add `text-pretty` to the description class list at page-header.tsx:238.

findings.title: Template editor (code review): mixed 'placeholder' and 'data otomatis' wording, a vague section title, a colour-only cue
findings.description: Not captured; reviewed from code. Structurally the screen conforms: AppPage with a three-level trail, h1 set to the template name, the sticky SettingsSaveBar, a two-pane layout with a sticky preview, and not-found, error and loading states. The copy is uneven. The UI calls substitutions 'data otomatis' ('Sisipkan data otomatis', 'Data otomatis yang dipakai'), but knownPlaceholdersEmpty says 'Placeholder yang ditulis ...', the body hint shows the raw token '{{nama_placeholder}}', and the field is labelled 'Isi (HTML)'. The first section is titled just 'Templat'. unknownPlaceholdersHint relies on colour alone ('Yang berwarna kuning ...'). While the list loads, the h1 and the last crumb read 'Ubah templat', then switch to the template's name.
findings.cause: apps/web/messages/features/documents.id.json editor.{knownPlaceholdersEmpty, bodyHint, bodyLabel, detailsTitle, unknownPlaceholdersHint}. apps/web/features/documents/components/template-editor.tsx:88 falls back to editor.editTitle while query.isLoading.
findings.fix: Use 'data otomatis' throughout, e.g. knownPlaceholdersEmpty: 'Jenis dokumen ini belum punya data otomatis dari sistem. Tulisan dalam kurung kurawal akan tampil apa adanya.' Retitle detailsTitle to 'Detail templat'. Say what the yellow badge means in words: 'Data yang ditandai Tidak dikenal akan tampil apa adanya', with Badge text or an icon for unknown items. While loading, pass `title` as a Skeleton or keep the trail without the last crumb instead of 'Ubah templat'.

baseline.note: The section Select and the 'Persiapan Sekolah' row are gone, and the description now sits in the header. On desktop the card starts at y=327 instead of 417. On the phone, WhatsApp still stacks the area tabs and the Penyedia/Templat/Log pills as two tab rows, and the first input starts about 507 of 844px down (finding -08).

Session, SSO, workflows and the template editor now share SettingsSaveBar with the unsaved-changes guard. The WhatsApp provider still has its own always-on 'Simpan' inside the card, with no dirty tracking (finding -03).

The badge has three states ('Belum diatur', 'Aktif', 'Tidak aktif'). The switch is hidden until configured, the save bar reads 'Simpan dan aktifkan', and required fields show errors in place. New issue: the status card's title now repeats the page title (finding -04).

The h1 'Keamanan akun' covers 2FA, passkeys and a link card to password and sessions. The 2FA card is titled by its feature with a status badge, and there is one primary button (passkey add is secondary). In code, the passkey name dialog has a labelled Field and footer buttons.

Stages are numbered collapsible rows with a 'who · how' summary. A Stepper summary sits beside them, the stage code is under 'Lanjutan', the label reads 'Jenis tugas', removal has an undo toast, and saving goes through the sticky bar with a new-version confirm. Remaining polish in findings -09 and -10.
StageEditor is rendered inside <TabsContent value={kind}> (workflow-definitions-view.tsx:206), and rows are keyed by stable client ids (stage-editor.tsx:172).

From code (the Templat tab was not captured): rows use 'Ubah' (templates-view.tsx:196), and the delete ConfirmDialog names the template in its description, with confirmLabel 'Hapus' and destructive set.

Content widths still differ (720 narrow, 672 WhatsApp provider, full-width workflows). Now the narrow pages are also centred while WhatsApp, workflows and audit are left-aligned, so the header and the section tabs jump 216px between sibling tabs (finding -01).

Save now shows a loading state and the switch moved off the left of its label. But the switch row floats mid-card in a 14rem label grid (finding -02), the panel tab is still defaultValue and not in the URL, and there is no connection check or test send (needs API).

apiNeeded: WhatsApp provider: an endpoint that verifies the credentials or sends a test message, so the Penyedia form can show connection status and offer 'Kirim pesan uji' (baseline pengaturan-platform-38).

Document templates: GET /v1/document-templates/{id}, so a deep link to /settings/document-templates/[templateId] does not need the whole list (template-editor.tsx:80 notes the API has no single-template read).

reviews.verdict: The rebuild of this area is real. /scan now opens on the camera in a framed viewfinder, with manual entry as a quiet fallback. /profile is one identity header with Akun, Data diri and Keamanan tabs on the narrow template. The /reports catalogue is a calm grid of icon cards: title first, the section strip under it, then a pill sub-switch. The kiosk frame for /monitor has a brand, a clock and no app chrome. Desktop light and dark both look clean and on-brand. Two things keep the unit from the owner's bar, both on a phone. On /notifications every older row is cut to "Pen…" / "Ada peng…" because the trailing full date takes the row's width (this is worse than before the overhaul), and the toolbar is shrink-wrapped so the search placeholder is cut and the controls stop two-thirds of the way across. The filled /inbox (guru) also pushes its only actionable request below the fold under three tall count tiles and a two-row chip filter that repeats the tiles' categories, and it uses a different search box and filter pattern from /notifications. The remaining issues are smaller: a 16px title drop on /reports for multi-section readers, export wording that says Excel when PDF is also offered, the profile avatar changing colour between the header and the page, and a 4:3 viewfinder that leaves a third of the phone screen empty.
best: /scan: camera first in a framed viewfinder with a hint pill and a quiet 'Masukkan kode manual' link; identical and tidy for every role on desktop and phone
/profile: one identity card (avatar, name, @username, role and school-year badges, Ganti foto) plus underline tabs on the 720px template; it replaces the old seven stacked boxes
/reports (admin, kepsek): h1 and description, underline section strip, pill 'Unduhan / Jadwal kirim', then a two-column grid of icon cards; the dark mode is clean
/notifications desktop: day groups, kind icons in soft circles, chevrons, unread tint, SegmentedControl instead of panel-less tabs
All-clear /inbox empty states now carry a way on ('Lihat riwayat izin' / 'Lihat surat peringatan')
worst: /notifications phone: titles and bodies truncated to 'Pen…', 'Sura…', 'Ada peng…' because the trailing time is the full '25 September 2026 pukul 19.01'
/notifications toolbar shrink-wrapped: search placeholder cut ('Cari judul atau isi notifi'), and search and select are only 242px wide on a 358px phone column
/inbox filled (guru, phone): three 130px count tiles, a hint, a search and a two-row chip filter come before the single request, and the tiles and chips repeat the same three categories
/reports: the whole page sits 16px lower for readers with several report sections; the copy says Excel only while the dialog offers PDF; the library section says 'Ekspor XLSX'

findings.title: Notification rows unreadable on a phone: the full date squeezes the title to 'Pen…'
findings.description: On a 390px phone every row older than a day reads 'Sura… / Surat izin…', 'Pen… / Pengaj izin…', 'Stat… / Status izin…' (siswa) and 'Pen… / Ada peng…' (guru). The trailing '25 September 2026 pukul 19.00' takes about 180px of the 260px text area. Today's row is cut too ('Pengajuan izin b…', next to '21 menit yang lalu'). Before the overhaul these rows were fully readable, so this is a regression. On desktop the same column repeats the date under a day heading that already says '25 September 2026' (old finding home-personal-29).
findings.cause: apps/web/features/notifications/components/notifications-view.tsx:262 passes formatRelative(...) as `trailing`. For anything older than 24h this returns formatDateTime (packages/i18n/src/format.ts:68-69). ListRow's trailing slot (packages/ui/src/components/list-row.tsx:197-202) is `display: contents` with `whitespace-nowrap` and `*:shrink-0`, so the long string never shrinks and the title and meta column (min-w-0 flex-1) collapses instead.
findings.fix: Rows sit under a day heading, so the trailing slot only needs the time. Use formatTime(item.created_at, { locale, timeZone }) for items not from today, and formatRelative only for today's items (better still, a short form such as '20 mnt'). Optionally, below sm, move the time into `meta` on its own caption line, as the bell panel already does (notification-panel.tsx:113-115).

findings.title: Notifications toolbar shrink-wrapped: placeholder cut, controls stop short of the column
findings.description: On desktop the search box is about 198px wide in a 720px column, and its placeholder is cut mid-word ('Cari judul atau isi notifi'). On a phone the search and the 'Semua jenis' select are both about 242px wide in a 358px column, leaving a 116px hole on the right ('Cari judul atau isi notifikas' is clipped there too). The segmented filter is also left at its own width. With 'Tandai semua dibaca' on its own row, a phone shows four stacked control rows (about 300px) before the first notification.
findings.cause: notifications-view.tsx:119 wraps the toolbar in `<div className="flex flex-col gap-3">`. PageShell drops that div into its `page-toolbar` slot, which is `flex flex-wrap items-center` (packages/ui/src/components/page-shell.tsx:146). As a flex item with no width it shrinks to its content, so `sm:flex-1` on the SearchInput (line 142) has no room to grow into. apps/web/features/visitors/components/gate-board-view.tsx:158 uses the same wrapper.
findings.fix: Change line 119 to `className="flex w-full flex-col gap-3"` (or `basis-full`). Give the SegmentedControl `fullWidth="phone"`. Move 'Tandai semua dibaca' from `actions` to `secondaryActions`, so it joins the header menu on a phone and the title row stays single. Apply the same `w-full` to gate-board-view.tsx:158.

findings.title: Filled inbox buries the one request under count tiles and a duplicate chip filter
findings.description: Guru /inbox on a phone shows, in order: the section header, a three-line hint, three StatTiles about 130px tall each ('1 Izin tidak masuk', '0 Izin keluar', and '0 Keterlambatan' stretched full width alone), a plain search input, and a chip filter that wraps to two rows ('Keterlambatan' alone on the second). The single actionable request starts at about 700px and its Setujui/Tolak buttons sit under the tab bar. The tiles and the chips name the same three categories. The search is a bare Input with no glass icon, unlike the SearchInput on /notifications, and the filter is a row of primary/secondary buttons where /notifications uses a SegmentedControl. On desktop the 130px tiles hold single digits in a lot of empty card.
findings.cause: apps/web/features/permits/components/permit-unified-queue.tsx: tiles at lines 233-248 (tileColumns gives 2+1 on phones, apps/web/lib/layout/bento.ts:54-60); a plain `<Input>` at 251; and `<div role="group" className="flex flex-wrap gap-2">` with Button toggles at 274-292. This component is used only by apps/web/features/inbox/components/action-inbox-view.tsx.
findings.fix: Drop the StatTile grid and render the kind filter as `<SegmentedControl size="sm" options={[{value:'all',...},...sources.map(s => ({ value: s.type, label: s.label, count: s.query.data?.data.length }))]} />`. That is one row, scrolling with fades on a phone, and it carries the counts. Replace the Input with `SearchInput` (with onClear). Put search and filter in one `flex w-full flex-col gap-2 sm:flex-row` row. Shorten or drop the queueHint paragraph, since the SectionHeader already names the queue.

findings.title: Reports hub page sits 16px lower than every other page; section tabs point at missing panels
findings.description: For readers with more than one report section (admin, kepsek) the eyebrow-less h1 'Laporan' sits at y≈112, against y≈96 for gurubk and wakepsek on the same route and for /inbox, /notifications and /scan. The phone shows the same 16px offset (102px against 86px). Between the 'Unduhan / Jadwal kirim' switch and the first card there is a 36px gap, where the rest of the template uses 16px. In code, only the selected section's TabsContent is rendered, so the inactive 'Laporan perpustakaan' and 'Rekap kunjungan' triggers keep aria-controls pointing at panels that do not exist. That is the axe aria-valid-attr-value violation the earlier audit found (home-personal-28).
findings.cause: apps/web/features/reports/components/reports-workspace-view.tsx:95 wraps the whole section page (AppPage included) in `<TabsContent value={selected.key}>`, and TabsContent adds `pt-4` (packages/ui/src/components/tabs.tsx:159). Only that one TabsContent is mounted. apps/web/features/reports/components/reports-view.tsx:73 adds `gap-5` on the inner Tabs on top of its TabsContent `pt-4`.
findings.fix: Pass `className="pt-0"` to the TabsContent at reports-workspace-view.tsx:95. Render one TabsContent per section, with the View only inside the selected one, so every trigger has its panel. Alternatively make the strip a `NavTabs` of `?section=` links, since it navigates. In reports-view.tsx set the inner Tabs to `gap-4` and its TabsContents to `pt-0`.

findings.title: Unread notifications are marked as the 'current' item
findings.description: Every unread row has the selected tint, and its link carries aria-current="true", so a screen reader announces each unread notification as 'current page'. ListRow's `selected` state is meant for the one open item of a master-detail list, not for unread.
findings.cause: apps/web/features/notifications/components/notifications-view.tsx:249 passes `selected={unread}`. ListRow then sets aria-current on its target (packages/ui/src/components/list-row.tsx:75, 82, 94) and paints `bg-state-selected` (line 138).
findings.fix: Drop `selected={unread}`. Show unread with the bold title the row already has, and either the coloured icon circle (already tone-switched) or a small accent dot in `trailing`. If a tint is still wanted, pass it through `className` (e.g. `bg-accent-soft/40`) without aria-current.

findings.title: Export wording says Excel or XLSX while the dialog also offers PDF; three verbs for one act
findings.description: The report centre description reads 'Unduh laporan sebagai berkas Excel.', and the library section's primary button reads 'Ekspor XLSX' (a raw format name). Both open the shared export dialog, which offers Excel and PDF. Across the hub's sections the same act is called 'Unduh' (cards), 'Ekspor XLSX' (library, primary) and 'Unduh rekap' (visitors, secondary). The library section is also the only one that makes it a primary button.
findings.cause: apps/web/messages/features/reports.id.json `description`; apps/web/messages/features/library.id.json `reports.exportXlsx` = 'Ekspor XLSX'. apps/web/components/report-export-dialog.tsx:324-325 lists both formats. apps/web/features/library/components/library-reports-view.tsx:157-166 renders it as primaryAction.
findings.fix: Reword the description to 'Unduh laporan sebagai berkas Excel atau PDF. Hanya laporan yang boleh dijalankan akun ini yang ditampilkan.' Rename `exportXlsx` to 'Unduh laporan'. Make it `secondaryActions` or a secondary button, so all three sections use one verb and one weight.

findings.title: Empty library report: orphan density and column icons, empty state with no way on
findings.description: Under 'Periode laporan', a row of two icon buttons (density and columns) floats alone at the far right, with nothing to configure, above an empty-state card. The empty state ('Tidak ada peminjaman pada rentang ini') offers no next step, such as widening the period.
findings.cause: packages/ui/src/components/data-table/data-table.tsx:400-415 always renders DataTableToolbar. The density and column toggles (data-table-toolbar.tsx:262-292) show even when the table is `empty` (data-table.tsx:351). apps/web/features/library/components/library-reports-view.tsx:325-327 passes an EmptyState without an action.
